text: The teacher who treated Harry Potter like dirt
spent the boy's whole life keeping him alive.
Severus Snape was a lonely kid in
a coat too big for him,
when he saw a girl make
a flower bloom in her hand.
Lily Evans.
He was the one who told
her she was a witch.
At Hogwarts, she went to Gryffindor.
He went to Slytherin,
and drifted toward the Dark Arts.
Then, humiliated in front of everyone,
he called her the one word
he could never take back.
She walked away.
He chose Voldemort.
He carried a prophecy to his master,
then realized who it pointed to.
Lily's son.
He begged Voldemort to spare her.
He begged Dumbledore to hide her.
It wasn't enough.
So he made a promise.
Protect the boy with her eyes.
That didn't make him kind.
He was cruel to Harry, cruel to Neville,
cruel to kids who couldn't fight back.
But he kept that promise.
When Dumbledore asked if he still loved her,
after all this time,
he answered with one word.
Always.
Dying, he asked Harry for one last thing.
Look at me.
Maybe so the last thing he
ever saw was her eyes.
